title: [finding] post-stamped reported read-back `identical` for a body the platform rewrote in 482 places — the one case read-back exists to catch
body:
Path: none | 仪器:`post-stamped` 对一次被平台改写 482 处的正文回读报 `identical` | 回读是它存在的理由

## One sentence

`scripts/pm/post-stamped.mjs` wrote a 105,390-character issue body, the platform stored a **117,948**-character one with **482** references rewritten, and the tool's read-back reported `"class": "identical"` — the one thing read-back exists to catch.

## Measured this round, ⛔ not recalled

Seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#6015, body write at 2026-09-20T12:09:22Z:

| reading | value |
|:--|--:|
| characters sent (the file handed to `--body=6015` on stdin) | **105,416** |
| `objectstack-ai/objectstack#` prefixes in what was sent | **1** |
| characters stored (fresh `GET` afterwards) | **117,948** |
| prefixes in what is stored | **483** |
| delta | **+12,532 chars = 482 × 26**, and `len('objectstack-ai/objectstack')` is exactly **26** |
| what `post-stamped --json` reported | `"body_landed": true`, `"read_back": {"class": "identical", "first_difference_byte": null}` |

⇒ every bare `#N` in the body was qualified to `objectstack-ai/objectstack#N` by something outside this tool, and the tool called the result identical.

## ⛔ The substance is fine — that is not what this card is about

Normalising the prefix away makes the two byte-identical (**105,390 = 105,390**), and the record written in that act is intact. The rewrite is lossless and points every reference where it already pointed; it is arguably what 〈多仓协调〉's 「裸 `#N` 改全名」 wants. **This card is about the instrument, not the damage** — a read-back that cannot distinguish "stored what I sent" from "stored something else that happens to be harmless" cannot be trusted the next time the difference is *not* harmless.

## The asymmetry, measured with a control

The rewrite is specific to **body** writes:

- **Body** (`--body=6015`): 482 references qualified.
- **Comment** (`--comment=13515`, `issuecomment-5749038121`, same session, same tool): the stored text carries **8** bare `#18336` references and **0** qualified prefixes — verbatim except the `{{NOW}}` substitution the tool declares.

⇒ lit control both ways: the write path is not qualifying anything, and the body path is. ⛔ The mechanism is not identified here — `grep` over `post-stamped.mjs` finds no such rewrite, so it is upstream of the tool (platform or relay), and naming it is the taker's first job.

⚠️ A second reading bounds it further: the six cards moved into objectui by **web-UI transfer** this round still carry **13** bare `#N` references. So a transferred body is **not** rewritten. ⇒ the rewrite happens on write through this channel, not on storage or on move.

## Why it matters to the fleet

The seat protocol leans on read-back everywhere: 「多席可写面恒读回;API 200 不等于落地正确」, and `post-stamped`'s own help promises exit **4 WRITTEN BUT NOT STORED — go read the artefact**. A seat that gets `identical` stops looking. Had this rewrite corrupted a `Restart-when:` predicate, a `Blocked-by:` line or a quoted ruling, the tool would have said the same word.

## Two shapes the fix could take, ⛔ neither chosen here

1. Compare against a **re-read**, and report a normalised-equal result as its own class (e.g. `platform-normalised`, naming the transformation) rather than folding it into `identical`.
2. If the comparison already normalises, say so in the status line and in `--help`, so `identical` stops meaning two different things.

## Dedupe

`post-stamped read-back identical` · `body reference qualification` · `objectstack-ai/objectstack# prefix rewrite` · `read_back class identical mutated`. Searched the 986 open cards of both boards for `read_back` / `read-back` / `identical` / `qualif` against a lit control (`post-stamped` → hits): no card carries this signature. #19236 (footer blank-line collapse, now fixed by `f93beea0a6`) is the same tool and a **different** transformation — that one the read-back *did* report.
